title: The Deception of Tamar and the Lineage of Christ
english: To her. But she had not seen him before, except that she had taken the ring, the cord, and the staff. As soon as he had intercourse with her, he went to his own pastures; but she, having changed back into the widow's clothes, was hiding unnoticed.

After Judas had sent away the servant, the servant searched for the cord and the things following, and did not find them; he was being torn by the absurdity, but he was enduring, desiring to see the deception fully. After time had passed, Tamar became pregnant, and Judah, having heard that she had conceived through fornication, commanded that she be burned alive.

But the woman being led away sends to Judah the cord, the ring, and the staff, saying: 'From the man to whom these belong, I have conceived; therefore recognize whose the ring is, and the cord, and the staff.' And Judah, mocking at the matter, and then becoming enraged, was reproaching himself for the injustice, saying: 'She is justified, or I, because of whom I did not give her to my son Shelah.'

But she, having given birth, brought forth twins in delivering. And the elder, that is, the first, put forth his hand, and the midwife tied red wool to his hand, saying: 'This one will come out first'; and immediately the child drew his hand inward, and his brother came out first and his name was called Perez; and after this the brother came out, on whom the red was in the hand, and he was named Zerah. Of these Joseph was a descendant, the one who remembers the immaculate Mary, from whom Christ took his flesh.

For Perez, as the evangelist Matthew recounts (Matt 1:3), begat Esrron, and Esrron begat Aram, and Aram begat Aminadab, and Aminadab begat Naasson, and Naasson begat Salmon, and Salmon begat Booz, and Booz begat Obed from Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon from the woman of Uriah, and Solomon begat Rehoboam, and Rehoboam begat Abijah, and Abijah begat Asa, and Asa begat Jehoshaphat; and Jehoshaphat begat Joram, and Joram begat Ozias, and Ozias begat Jehoiakim, and Jehoiakim begat Jeconias and his brothers during the deportation to Babylon; and after the deportation to Babylon, Jeconias begat Salathiel, and Salathiel begat Zorobabel, and Zorobabel begat Abiud, and Abiud begat Eliakim, and Eliakim begat Azor, and Azor begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Achim, and Achim begat Eliud, and Eliud begat Eleazar, and Eleazar begat Matthan, and Matthan begat Jacob, and Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus who is called the Christ (Matt 1:16). All the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations, and from David to the deportation to Babylon are fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ are fourteen generations.

It is necessary for us to seek by what kind of logic Matthew and Luke disagree (Luke 3:23) concerning Joseph in the genealogy: the one writes Jacob as the son of Matthan, but Luke writes him the son of Heli of Melchi; and how these, being of different generations, both Melchi and Matthan appear as grandfathers of Joseph. This is therefore being made clear. For first Matthan, the one of the lineage of Solomon, takes a wife named Ethan, and from this he begets Jacob, and dies. And Melchi, the one of the lineage of Matthan, takes her, and produces from her Heli. And so then both Matthan and Melchi, having taken the same woman, are two half-brothers.
